subject: Municipal Financial Interest Disclosure Provisions
overview: The subcommittee explored incorporating financial disclosure requirements for candidates and officials into the city charter, reviewing models from other Massachusetts municipalities. The group discussed whether to mandate these requirements directly in the charter or to establish an independent ethics commission via ordinance.

items.title: Municipal Charter Research
items.summary: Eunice Browne presented research showing that Framingham is unique among surveyed cities for including financial disclosure requirements directly in its charter.

items.title: Ordinance vs. Charter Implementation
items.summary: The group noted that most peer cities, including Boston, Cambridge, and Springfield, manage ethics disclosures through ordinances rather than charter mandates.

items.title: Candidate Recruitment and Privacy
items.summary: Members discussed whether requiring extensive 42-page state-style financial disclosure forms would discourage residents from running for local office.

items.title: Springfield Ethics Commission Model
items.summary: The subcommittee reviewed Springfield's manual, which uses a local ethics commission to administer conduct standards and financial interest filings.

items.title: Charter Mandate for Ethics Commission
items.summary: The group considered a proposal to include a charter provision requiring the city to establish an ethics commission by ordinance, with members appointed by the Mayor, City Council, and School Committee.

items.title: Assigned Research and Outreach
items.summary: Members agreed to contact other municipalities for sample forms and reach out to the city human resources director for feedback on how disclosures impact recruitment.

items.title: Meeting Scheduling
items.summary: The next subcommittee meeting was tentatively scheduled for July 15, 2024.
